contract_review.body:
# Status: reviewed conditional contracts — 2026-11-16

## Decision and scope

The project owner has accepted the clinical work and authorized resolving the P2 medication blockers. This review preserves that acceptance and the previous phenytoin adoption; it does not ask for the same authorization again. The exact contract IDs remain `status-phenytoin-local` and `status-refractory`. The former is a compatibility identifier, not a requirement to work in a particular hospital or jurisdiction.

These two contracts now have implementable, bounded outputs. Phenytoin offers a dose/time calculation and, separately, an optional product-specific preparation calculation. Refractory status offers specialist decision support, including escalation when resources are unavailable. Neither change asserts prospective clinical validation or an independently authenticated Pharmacy signature. The project's `CLINICALLY_PENDING` status and unrelated safety gates are preserved.

The recorded acceptance is carried by `acute-contract-owner-acceptance-2026-11-16.json`. Earlier provenance remains in the status owner acceptance of 2026-11-13 and the phenytoin preflight branch `review/status-phenytoin-preflight-20261115`, commit `4dcd6903c50910327e95c4b29d9d5909434f212e`. Its three historical files are:

- `clinical/qa/STATUS_PHENYTOIN_LOCAL_PRECLINICAL_GATE_2026-11-15.md`
- `clinical/scripts/status_phenytoin_local_preflight.py`
- `clinical/tests/test_status_phenytoin_local_preflight.py`

That preflight was deliberately disconnected from the API. Its historical NO-GO wording and always-blocked return do not override the later owner-authorized conditional release described here. The new helper does not import or silently change those historical files.

## Primary sources checked on 2026-11-16

| Source | Identified version and applicability | Use in these contracts |
|---|---|---|
| [Medinfo Galway: Phenytoin Intravenous for Adults](https://www.medinfogalway.ie/ivguides/phenytoin-intravenous-adults) | Live institutional IV guide; no page revision date is displayed. Its bibliography includes the Epanutin SPC of March 2023, Medusa accessed March 2024, and the adult GUH algorithm of March 2023. | The previously adopted adult initial loading regimen; a separately selected preparation profile for the exact products listed there. It is not a universal product label. |
| [NICE NG217, chapter 7](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng217/chapter/treating-status-epilepticus-repeated-or-cluster-seizures-and-prolonged-seizures) | NG217, updated 30 January 2025; recommendations 7.1.8–7.1.11. | After adequate initial treatment, IV second-line options and expert-led further treatment. Failure of one second-line option may lead to another under expert guidance; phenobarbital or general anaesthesia requires expert management. No numeric anaesthetic regimen is inferred. |
| [Intensive Care Society: acute management of adult status epilepticus](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12062632/) | Published 8 May 2025; *J Intensive Care Society* 26(2):249–262, DOI [10.1177/17511437251321338](https://doi.org/10.1177/17511437251321338). Scope: patients over 16 years, excluding obstetric presentations. | Refractory-stage identification, early critical-care involvement, EEG and referral/transfer. The implemented subset is adults aged 18 years or older and excludes obstetric management. |
| [Phenytoin Hospira 50 mg/mL SmPC](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/3794/smpc) | UK product information, eMC update 8 July 2026. | Product-specific contraindications and evidence that equal concentration does not establish preparation/regimen equivalence. Its adult loading recommendation of 10–15 mg/kg and its preparation instructions differ from the adopted Galway profile. It is not substituted into the Galway pump calculation. |

The international policy in `international-guideline-policy.md` applies: one canonical clinical module, with justified, complete source-specific choices. A dose source, a product label and an organization's operational capabilities are different kinds of evidence. Selecting this regimen does not declare it universally preferable, combine incompatible regimens or impose a hospital on the rest of Emergency.

## Phenytoin: two explicit capabilities

Both modes require adult age, verified weight, a clinician-confirmed convulsive indication after adequate benzodiazepine treatment, assessment of contraindications/interactions, available monitoring, and confirmation that the selected initial loading regimen is appropriate. Prior phenytoin/fosphenytoin exposure or maintenance therapy is outside this initial-load calculator: it requires a separate assessment rather than an automatic repeat. Cause-specific exceptions likewise do not receive this automatic loading result.

The selected calculation is:

```
dose_mg = 20 × min(weight_kg, 100)
rate_mg_min = dose_mg / selected_duration_min
```

The 2,000 mg cap is part of this selected regimen. The minimum duration of 40 minutes records the owner's preceding adoption decision; Galway itself does not impose a universal 40-minute minimum. The selected duration must respect the individual rate limit. This implementation adds a conservative maximum selected rate of 25 mg/min for an explicitly identified elderly/cardiac-risk patient; slower administration or a different dose/regimen may still be necessary. This is a bounded implementation rule, not a claim that every such patient has one universally correct rate.

### `dose_only`

The result contains mg, the selected duration and the corresponding mg/min. Product, withdrawal volume, final concentration, dilution, pump setting and stability are absent. The patient may therefore use a product not listed in the optional preparation profile, provided the clinician has verified that this selected dosing regimen applies; that product still needs its own preparation assessment before use.

For example, 100 kg at a selected maximum of 25 mg/min requires at least 80 minutes for this 2 g dose. Dose-only mode may represent that arithmetic without inventing a product's stability. It does not authorize preparing or infusing a mixture whose stability cannot accommodate it.

### `verified_preparation`

This optional profile requires the exact Epanutin or Mercury 250 mg/5 mL product listed by Galway, with documented correspondence between the actual product and the complete procedure. Equal concentration alone is insufficient; 100 mg/2 mL or another manufacturer's product is not automatically interchangeable.

The profile's source-bound values are: stock 50 mg/mL, NaCl 0.9% only, final concentration at most 10 mg/mL, maximum rate 50 mg/min, 5-micron drawing-up filter and 0.2-micron inline filter. Its saline table is:

| Dose | Verified NaCl volume before drug addition |
|---|---:|
| Below 500 mg | 50 mL |
| 500–1,000 mg inclusive | 100 mL |
| Above 1,000 mg | 250 mL |

The guide requires immediate initiation and completion within 60 minutes, a large-vein access, ECG/BP monitoring plus respiratory/site observation, clear solution, and saline flushing before/after. The final flush delivers residual drug at the same infusion rate. These are preparation-specific requirements, not global stability rules for all phenytoin products.

The implementation requires actual saline and final volumes to be independently verified, including the handling of bag overfill. It does not silently infer the final volume from the nominal bag label. Within this additive preparation the cross-check is `final_volume = verified_saline_volume + dose / 50`; a discrepancy stops the pump calculation instead of adapting the preparation.

```
pump_ml_h = verified_final_volume_ml × 60 / selected_duration_min
flush_duration_min = selected_duration_min × verified_post_flush_ml / verified_final_volume_ml
completion_min = elapsed_since_preparation_min + selected_duration_min + flush_duration_min
```

The post-flush volume is a required, verified case input, not a volume invented by this project. Counting the time needed to deliver residual drug through the line is an explicit conservative implementation of the completion limit. Exactly 60 minutes is allowed, subject only to floating-point representation tolerance; the older preflight's strict less-than-60 buffer is not misrepresented as a manufacturer stability limit. The elapsed-time check is not permission to delay the required immediate start or store the mixture. A timing conflict stops this preparation; the calculator never accelerates the infusion to satisfy expiry.

Manual acceptance example: 70 kg gives 1,400 mg; over 40 minutes this is 35 mg/min. Withdrawal from a verified 50 mg/mL product is 28 mL. Adding this to a measured 250 mL saline volume gives a verified final 278 mL and 417 mL/h. A verified 20 mL final flush at the same pump rate takes about 2.878 minutes; the total from an immediate start is about 42.878 minutes. This example is synthetic verification, not a default flush-volume recommendation.

## Refractory status: specialized decisions without an invented prescription

The decision workflow requires a non-obstetric adult after adequate benzodiazepine and second-line treatment. Ongoing convulsions or documented electrographic seizures support the entered refractory state. Continued impairment of consciousness without visible convulsions instead prompts urgent assessment and EEG; it is not automatically labelled non-convulsive status. An electrographic claim without EEG evidence is rejected.

The ICU consensus supports early critical-care review after adequate treatment fails, continuous EEG for refractory cases or persisting depressed consciousness, and specialist advice about management/transfer if EEG is unavailable. The contract translates that guidance into explicit actions determined by actual resources. Missing monitoring, airway expertise, critical care or EEG does not block access to the escalation instructions. It triggers the relevant support/transfer action and cannot enable an anaesthetic infusion.

The result is `result_kind=decision_support`, `treatment_calculated=false`. Medication dose, administration volume, duration and pump rate are all null. The expert team selects any additional antiseizure drug or anaesthetic regimen, with the necessary airway, haemodynamic and EEG support. The project does not turn a referral decision into a medication order.

## Interface and verification

`acute_reviewed_status.py` supplies exactly these two replacement rows through `reviewed_contracts(contract, field)`. Both identify this reference through `review_reference` and the dispatcher through `reviewed_workflow=status`. Common fields come from the canonical contract constructor. The compatibility key `local_protocol_verified` now means verifying the selected guidance and clinical context; it does not require a local hospital protocol.

The `calculation_scope` choice drives `required_if` for preparation fields. The API validates the active fields' types, expected values and boundaries. Missing active data cannot produce a result. Non-null data from an inactive preparation mode are rejected so an export cannot retain a hidden stale preparation. The helper adds cross-field checks, not a second type validator. Source revision hashes and faithful export checks remain the responsibility of the canonical API.

`test_acute_reviewed_status.py` provides explicit, independent browser fixtures and tests for both phenytoin modes and refractory decision support. It checks active missing inputs, populations, prior drugs, contraindications, numeric limits, product/diluent/filter mismatch, the 500/1,000 mg dilution boundaries, the 2 g cap, actual volume, rate/time conflicts, exact 60-minute completion including flushing, resource gaps, EEG-state consistency and export semantics. Test success establishes the stated functional behavior only.

# Status: reviewed conditional contracts — 2026-11-16

## Decision and scope

The project owner has accepted the clinical work and authorized resolving the P2 medication blockers. This review preserves that acceptance and the previous phenytoin adoption; it does not ask for the same authorization again. The exact contract IDs remain `status-phenytoin-local` and `status-refractory`. The former is a compatibility identifier, not a requirement to work in a particular hospital or jurisdiction.

These two contracts now have implementable, bounded outputs. Phenytoin offers a dose/time calculation and, separately, an optional product-specific preparation calculation. Refractory status offers specialist decision support, including escalation when resources are unavailable. Neither change asserts prospective clinical validation or an independently authenticated Pharmacy signature. The project's `CLINICALLY_PENDING` status and unrelated safety gates are preserved.

The recorded acceptance is carried by `acute-contract-owner-acceptance-2026-11-16.json`. Earlier provenance remains in the status owner acceptance of 2026-11-13 and the phenytoin preflight branch `review/status-phenytoin-preflight-20261115`, commit `4dcd6903c50910327e95c4b29d9d5909434f212e`. Its three historical files are:

- `clinical/qa/STATUS_PHENYTOIN_LOCAL_PRECLINICAL_GATE_2026-11-15.md`
- `clinical/scripts/status_phenytoin_local_preflight.py`
- `clinical/tests/test_status_phenytoin_local_preflight.py`

That preflight was deliberately disconnected from the API. Its historical NO-GO wording and always-blocked return do not override the later owner-authorized conditional release described here. The new helper does not import or silently change those historical files.

## Primary sources checked on 2026-11-16

| Source | Identified version and applicability | Use in these contracts |
|---|---|---|
| [Medinfo Galway: Phenytoin Intravenous for Adults](https://www.medinfogalway.ie/ivguides/phenytoin-intravenous-adults) | Live institutional IV guide; no page revision date is displayed. Its bibliography includes the Epanutin SPC of March 2023, Medusa accessed March 2024, and the adult GUH algorithm of March 2023. | The previously adopted adult initial loading regimen; a separately selected preparation profile for the exact products listed there. It is not a universal product label. |
| [NICE NG217, chapter 7](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng217/chapter/treating-status-epilepticus-repeated-or-cluster-seizures-and-prolonged-seizures) | NG217, updated 30 January 2025; recommendations 7.1.8–7.1.11. | After adequate initial treatment, IV second-line options and expert-led further treatment. Failure of one second-line option may lead to another under expert guidance; phenobarbital or general anaesthesia requires expert management. No numeric anaesthetic regimen is inferred. |
| [Intensive Care Society: acute management of adult status epilepticus](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12062632/) | Published 8 May 2025; *J Intensive Care Society* 26(2):249–262, DOI [10.1177/17511437251321338](https://doi.org/10.1177/17511437251321338). Scope: patients over 16 years, excluding obstetric presentations. | Refractory-stage identification, early critical-care involvement, EEG and referral/transfer. The implemented subset is adults aged 18 years or older and excludes obstetric management. |
| [Phenytoin Hospira 50 mg/mL SmPC](https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/3794/smpc) | UK product information, eMC update 8 July 2026. | Product-specific contraindications and evidence that equal concentration does not establish preparation/regimen equivalence. Its adult loading recommendation of 10–15 mg/kg and its preparation instructions differ from the adopted Galway profile. It is not substituted into the Galway pump calculation. |

The international policy in `international-guideline-policy.md` applies: one canonical clinical module, with justified, complete source-specific choices. A dose source, a product label and an organization's operational capabilities are different kinds of evidence. Selecting this regimen does not declare it universally preferable, combine incompatible regimens or impose a hospital on the rest of Emergency.

## Phenytoin: two explicit capabilities

Both modes require adult age, verified weight, a clinician-confirmed convulsive indication after adequate benzodiazepine treatment, assessment of contraindications/interactions, available monitoring, and confirmation that the selected initial loading regimen is appropriate. Prior phenytoin/fosphenytoin exposure or maintenance therapy is outside this initial-load calculator: it requires a separate assessment rather than an automatic repeat. Cause-specific exceptions likewise do not receive this automatic loading result.

The selected calculation is:

```
dose_mg = 20 × min(weight_kg, 100)
rate_mg_min = dose_mg / selected_duration_min
```

The 2,000 mg cap is part of this selected regimen. The minimum duration of 40 minutes records the owner's preceding adoption decision; Galway itself does not impose a universal 40-minute minimum. The selected duration must respect the individual rate limit. This implementation adds a conservative maximum selected rate of 25 mg/min for an explicitly identified elderly/cardiac-risk patient; slower administration or a different dose/regimen may still be necessary. This is a bounded implementation rule, not a claim that every such patient has one universally correct rate.

### `dose_only`

The result contains mg, the selected duration and the corresponding mg/min. Product, withdrawal volume, final concentration, dilution, pump setting and stability are absent. The patient may therefore use a product not listed in the optional preparation profile, provided the clinician has verified that this selected dosing regimen applies; that product still needs its own preparation assessment before use.

For example, 100 kg at a selected maximum of 25 mg/min requires at least 80 minutes for this 2 g dose. Dose-only mode may represent that arithmetic without inventing a product's stability. It does not authorize preparing or infusing a mixture whose stability cannot accommodate it.

### `verified_preparation`

This optional profile requires the exact Epanutin or Mercury 250 mg/5 mL product listed by Galway, with documented correspondence between the actual product and the complete procedure. Equal concentration alone is insufficient; 100 mg/2 mL or another manufacturer's product is not automatically interchangeable.

The profile's source-bound values are: stock 50 mg/mL, NaCl 0.9% only, final concentration at most 10 mg/mL, maximum rate 50 mg/min, 5-micron drawing-up filter and 0.2-micron inline filter. Its saline table is:

| Dose | Verified NaCl volume before drug addition |
|---|---:|
| Below 500 mg | 50 mL |
| 500–1,000 mg inclusive | 100 mL |
| Above 1,000 mg | 250 mL |

The guide requires immediate initiation and completion within 60 minutes, a large-vein access, ECG/BP monitoring plus respiratory/site observation, clear solution, and saline flushing before/after. The final flush delivers residual drug at the same infusion rate. These are preparation-specific requirements, not global stability rules for all phenytoin products.

The implementation requires actual saline and final volumes to be independently verified, including the handling of bag overfill. It does not silently infer the final volume from the nominal bag label. Within this additive preparation the cross-check is `final_volume = verified_saline_volume + dose / 50`; a discrepancy stops the pump calculation instead of adapting the preparation.

```
pump_ml_h = verified_final_volume_ml × 60 / selected_duration_min
flush_duration_min = selected_duration_min × verified_post_flush_ml / verified_final_volume_ml
completion_min = elapsed_since_preparation_min + selected_duration_min + flush_duration_min
```

The post-flush volume is a required, verified case input, not a volume invented by this project. Counting the time needed to deliver residual drug through the line is an explicit conservative implementation of the completion limit. Exactly 60 minutes is allowed, subject only to floating-point representation tolerance; the older preflight's strict less-than-60 buffer is not misrepresented as a manufacturer stability limit. The elapsed-time check is not permission to delay the required immediate start or store the mixture. A timing conflict stops this preparation; the calculator never accelerates the infusion to satisfy expiry.

Manual acceptance example: 70 kg gives 1,400 mg; over 40 minutes this is 35 mg/min. Withdrawal from a verified 50 mg/mL product is 28 mL. Adding this to a measured 250 mL saline volume gives a verified final 278 mL and 417 mL/h. A verified 20 mL final flush at the same pump rate takes about 2.878 minutes; the total from an immediate start is about 42.878 minutes. This example is synthetic verification, not a default flush-volume recommendation.

## Refractory status: specialized decisions without an invented prescription

The decision workflow requires a non-obstetric adult after adequate benzodiazepine and second-line treatment. Ongoing convulsions or documented electrographic seizures support the entered refractory state. Continued impairment of consciousness without visible convulsions instead prompts urgent assessment and EEG; it is not automatically labelled non-convulsive status. An electrographic claim without EEG evidence is rejected.

The ICU consensus supports early critical-care review after adequate treatment fails, continuous EEG for refractory cases or persisting depressed consciousness, and specialist advice about management/transfer if EEG is unavailable. The contract translates that guidance into explicit actions determined by actual resources. Missing monitoring, airway expertise, critical care or EEG does not block access to the escalation instructions. It triggers the relevant support/transfer action and cannot enable an anaesthetic infusion.

The result is `result_kind=decision_support`, `treatment_calculated=false`. Medication dose, administration volume, duration and pump rate are all null. The expert team selects any additional antiseizure drug or anaesthetic regimen, with the necessary airway, haemodynamic and EEG support. The project does not turn a referral decision into a medication order.

## Interface and verification

`acute_reviewed_status.py` supplies exactly these two replacement rows through `reviewed_contracts(contract, field)`. Both identify this reference through `review_reference` and the dispatcher through `reviewed_workflow=status`. Common fields come from the canonical contract constructor. The compatibility key `local_protocol_verified` now means verifying the selected guidance and clinical context; it does not require a local hospital protocol.

The `calculation_scope` choice drives `required_if` for preparation fields. The API validates the active fields' types, expected values and boundaries. Missing active data cannot produce a result. Non-null data from an inactive preparation mode are rejected so an export cannot retain a hidden stale preparation. The helper adds cross-field checks, not a second type validator. Source revision hashes and faithful export checks remain the responsibility of the canonical API.

`test_acute_reviewed_status.py` provides explicit, independent browser fixtures and tests for both phenytoin modes and refractory decision support. It checks active missing inputs, populations, prior drugs, contraindications, numeric limits, product/diluent/filter mismatch, the 500/1,000 mg dilution boundaries, the 2 g cap, actual volume, rate/time conflicts, exact 60-minute completion including flushing, resource gaps, EEG-state consistency and export semantics. Test success establishes the stated functional behavior only.

monitoring_and_warnings: - Treat generalized convulsive status epilepticus for a seizure **lasting 5 minutes or more (>=5 minutes)** or recurrent seizures without recovery. Do not wait for 30 minutes. Stabilize airway/breathing/circulation, check glucose immediately, obtain IV/IO access, correct hypoxia/electrolytes and investigate toxins, infection, pregnancy/eclampsia, structural lesions and medication nonadherence in parallel.
- **First-line benzodiazepine — give a full effective dose promptly, not repeated small fractions.** If IV access and resuscitation facilities are available: lorazepam **0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg)**, may repeat once if seizure persists. Alternative: diazepam **0.15--0.2 mg/kg IV (max 10 mg)**, may repeat once. If no IV access: the AES studied IM midazolam regimen is **10 mg when >40 kg or 5 mg at 13--40 kg**, as a single initial dose; smaller children require their pediatric pathway. Prepare airway support before/while giving benzodiazepines; respiratory depression risk is real but undertreatment of status is also dangerous.
- **Established benzodiazepine-refractory status:** promptly give one adequately dosed IV second-line antiseizure medication. Current ED evidence supports clinical equipoise among:
  - levetiracetam **60 mg/kg IV, max 4,500 mg**;
  - fosphenytoin **20 mg PE/kg IV, max 1,500 mg PE**;
  - sodium valproate **40 mg/kg IV, max 3,000 mg**.
  ESETT infused each of these trial regimens over **10 minutes**; use the verified local preparation/product and monitored infusion protocol, not the trial vial concentration by assumption. Choose according to contraindications, interactions, pregnancy, liver disease, cardiac conduction disease and local availability; do not delay escalation searching for a theoretically superior agent.
- **Reviewed adult phenytoin alternative (owner acceptance reconfirmed 2026-11-16):** when selected instead of fosphenytoin for ongoing convulsive status after an adequate benzodiazepine, the initial loading reference is **20 mg/kg IV, maximum 2 g**. The project owner previously adopted administration over **at least 40 min**; this is a declared project choice, not a universal guideline requirement. Respect the individual maximum rate, never above **50 mg/min**, and slower rates where indicated; the reviewed contract conservatively requires **25 mg/min or less** in older patients or cardiac disease. Continuous ECG, blood pressure and respiratory monitoring are required. Previous phenytoin/fosphenytoin or maintenance exposure needs an individualized top-up assessment, not another automatic full load. Do not interchange phenytoin mg and fosphenytoin mg PE.
- **Dose and product preparation are separate capabilities:** the global dose/time pathway does not require a hospital identity. The optional verified-preparation calculation covers only the products and complete preparation explicitly described in the [reviewed status reference](../references/acute-status-reviewed-2026-11-16.md): actual diluent plus drug volume, exact final volume, product-specific filters, saline, immediate use and completion within the supported preparation window including residual-drug delivery. No nominal bag-volume assumption, foreign-product substitution or universal stability is inferred. A missing verified preparation prevents only the dependent mL/pump result.
- **Important selection boundaries:** avoid valproate where contraindicated (notably significant hepatic disease and pregnancy/people with childbearing potential unless specialist benefit clearly outweighs risk); use caution with fosphenytoin/phenytoin in bradycardia, AV block or major conduction disease. Levetiracetam is often operationally simpler but is not universally superior.
- If convulsive activity stops but consciousness does not recover as expected, suspect **non-convulsive status** and obtain urgent EEG/neurology input rather than assuming a postictal state.
- **Refractory status epilepticus:** after adequate benzodiazepine plus an adequate second-line load, involve ICU/neurology, secure airway as required, start continuous EEG and use an anesthetic-infusion pathway (e.g. midazolam/propofol/other specialist regimen) with hemodynamic and ventilation support. No single anesthetic strategy has definitive superiority.
- **Refractory workflow release (2026-11-16):** the previous permanent software block is replaced by structured decision support: confirm adequate prior treatment, distinguish continuing convulsions, EEG-confirmed seizures and failure to recover consciousness, activate specialist/ICU/airway support and establish EEG access or transfer. Resource gaps remain actionable findings; they do not hide the escalation workflow. This contract generates no universal anesthetic dose or pump setting. The owner's acceptance is recorded in the [acute contract release](../references/acute-contract-owner-acceptance-2026-11-16.json).
- Pregnancy/eclampsia, toxin-mediated seizures, alcohol withdrawal and severe metabolic disturbances require the corresponding cause-specific pathway; do not apply this generic algorithm without modification.
- Portugal/Azores: on 2026-11-13 the owner confirms all requested local requirements (drugs/preparations, EEG access/circuit and neurology/ICU escalation) and accepts the pathway. This declaration does not identify brands/concentrations or prove on-site continuous EEG; verify exact product and pump preparation for each administration and use the confirmed EEG/escalation circuit. No new independent pharmacy/neurology signature or prospective validation is inferred.

This implementation adds a conservative maximum selected rate of 25 mg/min for an explicitly identified elderly/cardiac-risk patient; slower administration or a different dose/regimen may still be necessary. This is a bounded implementation rule, not a claim that every such patient has one universally correct rate.

### `dose_only`

The result contains mg, the selected duration and the corresponding mg/min. Product, withdrawal volume, final concentration, dilution, pump setting and stability are absent. The patient may therefore use a product not listed in the optional preparation profile, provided the clinician has verified that this selected dosing regimen applies; that product still needs its own preparation assessment before use.

For example, 100 kg at a selected maximum of 25 mg/min requires at least 80 minutes for this 2 g dose. Dose-only mode may represent that arithmetic without inventing a product's stability. It does not authorize preparing or infusing a mixture whose stability cannot accommodate it.

### `verified_preparation`

This optional profile requires the exact Epanutin or Mercury 250 mg/5 mL product listed by Galway, with documented correspondence between the actual product and the complete procedure. Equal concentration alone is insufficient; 100 mg/2 mL or another manufacturer's product is not automatically interchangeable.

The profile's source-bound values are: stock 50 mg/mL, NaCl 0.9% only, final concentration at most 10 mg/mL, maximum rate 50 mg/min, 5-micron drawing-up filter and 0.2-micron inline filter. Its saline table is:

| Dose | Verified NaCl volume before drug addition |
|---|---:|
| Below 500 mg | 50 mL |
| 500–1,000 mg inclusive | 100 mL |
| Above 1,000 mg | 250 mL |

The guide requires immediate initiation and completion within 60 minutes, a large-vein access, ECG/BP monitoring plus respiratory/site observation, clear solution, and saline flushing before/after. The final flush delivers residual drug at the same infusion rate. These are preparation-specific requirements, not global stability rules for all phenytoin products.

The implementation requires actual saline and final volumes to be independently verified, including the handling of bag overfill. It does not silently infer the final volume from the nominal bag label. Within this additive preparation the cross-check is `final_volume = verified_saline_volume + dose / 50`; a discrepancy stops the pump calculation instead of adapting the preparation.

```
pump_ml_h = verified_final_volume_ml × 60 / selected_duration_min
flush_duration_min = selected_duration_min × verified_post_flush_ml / verified_final_volume_ml
completion_min = elapsed_since_preparation_min + selected_duration_min + flush_duration_min
```

The post-flush volume is a required, verified case input, not a volume invented by this project. Counting the time needed to deliver residual drug through the line is an explicit conservative implementation of the completion limit. Exactly 60 minutes is allowed, subject only to floating-point representation tolerance; the older preflight's strict less-than-60 buffer is not misrepresented as a manufacturer stability limit. The elapsed-time check is not permission to delay the required immediate start or store the mixture. A timing conflict stops this preparation; the calculator never accelerates the infusion to satisfy expiry.

Manual acceptance example: 70 kg gives 1,400 mg; over 40 minutes this is 35 mg/min. Withdrawal from a verified 50 mg/mL product is 28 mL. Adding this to a measured 250 mL saline volume gives a verified final 278 mL and 417 mL/h. A verified 20 mL final flush at the same pump rate takes about 2.878 minutes; the total from an immediate start is about 42.878 minutes. This example is synthetic verification, not a default flush-volume recommendation.

## Refractory status: specialized decisions without an invented prescription

The decision workflow requires a non-obstetric adult after adequate benzodiazepine and second-line treatment. Ongoing convulsions or documented electrographic seizures support the entered refractory state. Continued impairment of consciousness without visible convulsions instead prompts urgent assessment and EEG; it is not automatically labelled non-convulsive status. An electrographic claim without EEG evidence is rejected.

The ICU consensus supports early critical-care review after adequate treatment fails, continuous EEG for refractory cases or persisting depressed consciousness, and specialist advice about management/transfer if EEG is unavailable. The contract translates that guidance into explicit actions determined by actual resources. Missing monitoring, airway expertise, critical care or EEG does not block access to the escalation instructions. It triggers the relevant support/transfer action and cannot enable an anaesthetic infusion.

The result is `result_kind=decision_support`, `treatment_calculated=false`. Medication dose, administration volume, duration and pump rate are all null. The expert team selects any additional antiseizure drug or anaesthetic regimen, with the necessary airway, haemodynamic and EEG support. The project does not turn a referral decision into a medication order.

## Interface and verification

`acute_reviewed_status.py` supplies exactly these two replacement rows through `reviewed_contracts(contract, field)`. Both identify this reference through `review_reference` and the dispatcher through `reviewed_workflow=status`. Common fields come from the canonical contract constructor. The compatibility key `local_protocol_verified` now means verifying the selected guidance and clinical context; it does not require a local hospital protocol.

The `calculation_scope` choice drives `required_if` for preparation fields. The API validates the active fields' types, expected values and boundaries. Missing active data cannot produce a result. Non-null data from an inactive preparation mode are rejected so an export cannot retain a hidden stale preparation. The helper adds cross-field checks, not a second type validator. Source revision hashes and faithful export checks remain the responsibility of the canonical API.

`test_acute_reviewed_status.py` provides explicit, independent browser fixtures and tests for both phenytoin modes and refractory decision support. It checks active missing inputs, populations, prior drugs, contraindications, numeric limits, product/diluent/filter mismatch, the 500/1,000 mg dilution boundaries, the 2 g cap, actual volume, rate/time conflicts, exact 60-minute completion including flushing, resource gaps, EEG-state consistency and export semantics. Test success establishes the stated functional behavior only.

actual.compatibility: Vía IM exclusivamente en este contrato. No diluir a 0,1 mg/mL ni usar la bolsa IV de 10 microgramos/mL.
actual.stability: Producto íntegro y vigente; uso inmediato tras apertura según su ficha. No se asigna vida útil a una dilución.
actual.administration: IM en tercio medio anterolateral del muslo. Reevaluar y repetir a los 5 min si persiste compromiso ABC. Antes de 5 min, este contrato ofrece orientación sin dosificación; la actuación urgente sigue la decisión médica individual.
limitations: Pauta seleccionada ERC 2025/WAO 2020; la banda RCUK de 100–150 microgramos para menores de 6 meses es una discrepancia explícita, no un mínimo ni una dosis que se promedie.

El formulario comprueba el cálculo y el dispositivo declarado; no acredita exactitud física, peso plausible ni diagnóstico. Confirmar especialmente neonatos y prematuros, sin retrasar tratamiento necesario.
No cubre reanimación al nacimiento, parada cardíaca, autoinyectores ni otras vías. La valoración de riesgos relativos no equivale a contraindicar adrenalina IM en anafilaxia.

Tras dos dosis adecuadas y compromiso persistente, activar ayuda experta; puede continuar IM mientras se prepara una perfusión segura. No continuar IM automáticamente cuando la perfusión esté en marcha.
next_actions: Reevaluar ABC y respuesta; registrar dosis y hora reales. No generar repeticiones automáticas.
actual.monitoring_and_warnings:
- Diagnose clinically when there is sudden compatible **airway, breathing or circulation compromise**, with or without skin/mucosal findings, after a likely trigger. Skin signs may be absent. Remove/stop the trigger if immediately feasible and call for resuscitation help.
- **Adrenaline (epinephrine) IM is first-line.** Inject into the anterolateral thigh using **1 mg/mL (1:1000)** solution. RCUK/ERC 2025 adult dose: **500 micrograms IM (0.5 mL)**. Repeat after **5 min** if airway/breathing/circulation problems persist.
- Pediatric age-banded IM doses from the RCUK full anaphylaxis guideline (2021, still the latest full guideline on the official current listing; distinct from the 2025 special-circumstances update): >12 y **500 micrograms**; 6--12 y **300 micrograms**; 6 months--6 y **150 micrograms**; <6 months **100--150 micrograms**. Use weight/local pediatric charts when available and independently double-check small-volume doses.
- **Reviewed IM pathway for infants under 6 months (owner acceptance 2026-11-16):** for clinically diagnosed acute anaphylaxis with ongoing airway/breathing/circulation compromise, use verified current weight: **0.01 mg/kg = 10 micrograms/kg = 0.01 mL/kg of UNDILUTED 1 mg/mL adrenaline**, injected into the anterolateral mid-thigh. This selects the weight-based recommendation in [ERC Paediatric Life Support 2025](https://www.erc.edu/media/03xnpjmj/gl2025-09-pls-e.pdf) and [WAO Anaphylaxis Guidance 2020](https://www.worldallergyorganizationjournal.org/article/S1939-4551%2820%2930375-6/fulltext). The general single-dose ceiling is 0.5 mg; it is not a minimum or an expected infant dose. The RCUK <6-month band of **100--150 micrograms** remains a documented alternative, not a floor imposed on the weight-based calculation. Reassess at 5 min; an earlier repeat is an individual expert decision outside this numerical regimen. The software keeps urgent decision support accessible but supplies no calculated repeat dose before 5 min. Confirm a device capable of accurately delivering the exact volume; no automatic rounding or dilution. **Do not dilute this IM dose to 0.1 mg/mL**: that concentration belongs to separate IV pathways. Neonatal anaphylaxis requires individual assessment; this contract does not cover resuscitation at birth or cardiac arrest. Two appropriate IM doses with continuing compromise trigger expert refractory assessment, while IM can continue as indicated until a safe infusion is running. Details and source reconciliation: [reviewed anaphylaxis contracts](../references/acute-anaphylaxis-reviewed-2026-11-16.md).
- **IM adrenaline has no absolute contraindication in anaphylaxis.** Review risks, interactions and product identity without delaying first-line treatment; relative contraindications must not become a blanket software stop.
- Position flat with or without leg elevation unless breathing difficulty requires sitting; in pregnancy use left lateral tilt/positioning as appropriate. Give high-flow oxygen and monitoring.
- **Fluids:** give IV isotonic crystalloid early for shock and reassess. RCUK adult reference bolus **500--1000 mL**; children **10 mL/kg**, repeated according to response and overload risk.
- Progressive airway edema requires early expert airway planning. Do not delay IM adrenaline while preparing the airway.
- **Refractory anaphylaxis:** persistent airway/breathing/circulation compromise after **2 appropriate IM adrenaline doses** should trigger the refractory-anaphylaxis pathway and expert **low-dose IV adrenaline infusion** with continuous monitoring. Avoid unmonitored IV adrenaline boluses.
- Antihistamines and corticosteroids are not substitutes for IM adrenaline in life-threatening anaphylaxis. Treat bronchospasm or other persistent features as adjuncts only after adrenaline/resuscitation priorities are addressed.
- **Accepted refractory infusion reference (owner acceptance 2026-11-13):** adrenaline **1 mg made up to a final volume of 100 mL with NaCl 0.9% = 10 micrograms/mL**. Start **0.5--1 mL/kg/h**, titrating to response at the lowest effective rate under experienced critical-care supervision. Calculation: 10 micrograms/mL x 0.5--1 mL/kg/h / 60 = **0.083--0.167 micrograms/kg/min**. Continue IM adrenaline every 5 min until the infusion is running. Prime the dedicated pump line; do not piggy-back or use the arm with a BP cuff. Continuous ECG/SpO2 and frequent BP, with regular cannula/extravasation checks, are mandatory. Product-specific preparation, stability and replacement interval remain subject to verification; acceptance does not certify these details.
- **Reviewed IV initiation (owner acceptance 2026-11-16):** the selected [RCUK 2021 section 6.6 regimen](https://www.resus.org.uk/sites/default/files/2021-05/Emergency%20Treatment%20of%20Anaphylaxis%20May%202021_0.pdf) applies to adults and children with persistent respiratory/circulatory compromise after two appropriate IM doses. Use **0.5 mL/kg/h for moderate severity** or **1 mL/kg/h for severe hypotensive/hypoxic presentations**, with the already specified **1 mg made up to a final volume of 100 mL** preparation. These equal **0.083333... and 0.166666... micrograms/kg/min** respectively. The calculation covers an expert-selected starting rate; it does not impose 1 mL/kg/h as a universal maintenance maximum or generate automatic titration. If the two preceding IM doses were separated by less than 5 min, provide urgent expert decision support without a calculated IV initiation rate. Verify actual prior doses/times, product-specific compatibility and use limit, pump, dedicated primed line, continuous ECG/SpO2, BP at least every 5 min and surveillance for extravasation. Details: [reviewed anaphylaxis contracts](../references/acute-anaphylaxis-reviewed-2026-11-16.md).
- **Observation/discharge (NICE NG258, 2026):** consider **2 h** observation after airway swelling has resolved and breathing, BP and HR have normalized only with a prompt response within 5--10 min to one IM dose administered within 30 min of onset, complete resolution, two in-date auto-injectors with demonstrated use and adequate adult supervision if needed. Observe at least **6 h after all symptoms resolve** if two IM doses were needed or there is previous biphasic anaphylaxis. Observe at least **12 h after all symptoms resolve** for severe reactions requiring >2 doses, severe asthma/respiratory compromise, continuing allergen absorption, out-of-hours presentation, inability to respond to deterioration or difficult emergency access. These are risk-based minima, not automatic discharge deadlines; refractory cases need critical-care assessment.
- Before discharge: provide written recurrence/emergency advice, trigger avoidance, two appropriate adrenaline auto-injectors with training when indicated and specialist allergy referral. The owner accepts this reference pathway on 2026-11-13; no named pharmacy sign-off, local stock audit or independently verified referral availability is inferred. The owner reconfirmed release of the reviewed contracts on 2026-11-16: the prior permanent software blocks are superseded by case-specific input, preparation and monitoring checks. This does not certify prospective clinical deployment.

contract_review.body:
# Anafilaxia: contratos revisados de IM en menores de 6 meses y perfusión IV

**Revisión focal: 16/11/2026.** Contratos: `anaphylaxis-under6months` y `anaphylaxis-refractory`. Núcleo internacional, sin país u hospital obligatorios. Aplicar [la política de guías internacionales](international-guideline-policy.md); las fuentes se seleccionan por alcance y calidad, no por la ubicación del propietario.

## Aceptación y procedencia

Juan ha autorizado resolver estos contratos y ha declarado su validación clínica en esta sesión. La presente entrega registra esa aceptación del propietario; no inventa una firma independiente de Farmacia/Pediatría, una auditoría de existencias ni una evaluación prospectiva. El estado global `CLINICALLY_PENDING` se conserva. Los controles individuales que se describen abajo siguen siendo necesarios.

Base comunicada por coordinación: `062d890b4fc92369b83c87664bb4bb0205ccb33f`, repositorio `JuanCopado/Emergency`. Se reutilizó material de:

- `review/anaphylaxis-under6months-evidence-20261116` en `e9855dbd37409189757c94900ee03e06ef25af3d`: conciliación de fuentes, acta funcional, preflight de microvolumen y revisión de selección de aguja. Su aclaración final diferencia IM sin diluir de la dilución IV de 1 mg hasta 10 mL.
- `review/anaphylaxis-refractory-20261116` en `0bff44dded89ea9da7f178ddf526d44969586c9c`: conciliación C04 y anexo pediátrico/pruebas negativas. La receta de perfusión ya figura en el módulo con aceptación del propietario de 13/11/2026.

Esos antecedentes documentaban cálculos o escenarios aún bloqueados. No se convierten retrospectivamente sus casos `NOT_RUN` en pruebas superadas. Esta entrega añade cálculo y comprobaciones propias; la integración en API/UI y la publicación se verifican por coordinación. Las exigencias históricas de un centro concreto no se trasladan al núcleo internacional.

## Fuentes primarias y decisión

| Fuente | Versión y uso en esta entrega |
|---|---|
| [ERC Paediatric Life Support](https://www.erc.edu/media/03xnpjmj/gl2025-09-pls-e.pdf) | 2025, Resuscitation 215:110767; sección de anafilaxia, p. 20. Fuente principal de la pauta IM ponderal y reevaluación/repetición a 5 min. Población pediátrica desde el nacimiento hasta 18 años; la reanimación al nacimiento pertenece a otro algoritmo. |
| [WAO Anaphylaxis Guidance](https://www.worldallergyorganizationjournal.org/article/S1939-4551%2820%2930375-6/fulltext) | 2020; tratamiento agudo y tabla 6. Respalda 0,01 mg/kg y ausencia de contraindicación absoluta para adrenalina IM en anafilaxia. Aporta alcance internacional; su intervalo de 5–15 min no sustituye el intervalo de 5 min seleccionado de ERC. |
| [RCUK Emergency treatment of anaphylaxis](https://www.resus.org.uk/sites/default/files/2021-05/Emergency%20Treatment%20of%20Anaphylaxis%20May%202021_0.pdf) | Mayo de 2021; tabla de dosis IM, sección 6.6 y apéndice 3. Pauta completa seleccionada para el inicio de perfusión en adultos y niños; discrepancia de banda IM por edad conservada. |
| [Listado oficial RCUK](https://www.resus.org.uk/library/additional-guidance/guidance-anaphylaxis/emergency-treatment-anaphylactic-reactions) | Consultado 16/11/2026: sigue identificando mayo de 2021 como edición completa más reciente. Describe uso por profesionales dentro y fuera del hospital. |
| [RCUK Paediatric emergency algorithms & resources](https://www.resus.org.uk/sites/default/files/2026-02/RCUK%20Paediatric%20emergency%20algorithms%20and%20resources%20Feb%2026%20V6.pdf) | Febrero de 2026, versión 6. Mantiene los algoritmos de anafilaxia y señala revisión de anafilaxia prevista en 2026; no equivale a una nueva guía completa de anafilaxia. |
| [AEMPS: Adrenalina Basi 1 mg/mL, registro 89175](https://cima.aemps.es/cima/dochtml/ft/89175/FT_89175.html) | Ficha consultada 16/11/2026, §§4.2–4.3 y 6.6: confirma la pauta IM ponderal en menores de 6 meses y distingue la dilución IV. Es información de un producto, no una aprobación universal de cualquier preparación ni disponibilidad. |
| [DailyMed: Adrenalin, set b293ad8e…](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=b293ad8e-7055-4a95-a130-9d7d74f19eab) | Etiqueta actualizada 22/10/2026. Su preparación IV para hipotensión por shock séptico no recomienda salino solo y tiene condiciones propias. Demuestra por qué no se extrapolan diluyentes/plazos a otra indicación, concentración o producto. |
| [ASCIA Acute Management of Anaphylaxis](https://www.allergy.org.au/images/ASCIA_HP_Guidelines_Acute_Management_Anaphylaxis_October_2026.pdf) | Edición de octubre de 2026 localizada en la [página oficial](https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/anaphylaxis/acute-management-guidelines). Se registra para vigilancia: no se afirma conciliación íntegra de sus figuras ni se introduce una pauta procedente de ellas en este helper. |

Esta revisión es focal y no acredita concordancia con todas las guías, fichas o jurisdicciones. Los errores de extracción de símbolos en PDF no se trasladan a código: **0,01 mg = 10 microgramos**, nunca 10 mg.

## Contrato IM: selección, cálculo y controles

Ámbito: anafilaxia aguda diagnosticada por el profesional con compromiso ABC persistente, edad cronológica **0 a menos de 6 meses** y peso actual verificado. No diagnostica automáticamente anafilaxia ni cubre parada cardíaca o reanimación al nacimiento. Los neonatos/prematuros precisan valoración individual y ayuda adecuada sin retrasar el tratamiento necesario.

Se selecciona **10 microgramos/kg IM de adrenalina 1 mg/mL SIN DILUIR**, en cara anterolateral del tercio medio del muslo. El techo general ERC/WAO es 500 microgramos por dosis; no es un mínimo ni una dosis esperada en un lactante. La banda RCUK de **100–150 microgramos** para menores de 6 meses queda explícita como otra recomendación. No se promedian las pautas, no se impone 100 microgramos como suelo y no se sustituye el cálculo por una edad de referencia.

Para peso `W` en kg:

`microgramos = min(10 × W, 500)`; `mg = microgramos / 1000`; `mL IM = mg / 1 mg/mL`.

Ejemplo sintético: **5 kg → 50 microgramos → 0,05 mg → 0,05 mL**. No diluir a **0,1 mg/mL** para facilitar la medida: 1 mg hasta 10 mL pertenece a un circuito IV distinto. Tampoco usar la perfusión de 10 microgramos/mL como preparación IM.

La medición requiere intervalo de entrega, capacidad, incremento y exactitud del dispositivo verificados. Se calcula con `Decimal`; si el volumen exacto no puede representarse, se detiene ese cálculo operativo para revisar el método de medida. No se autoriza redondeo, dosis mínima, dilución alternativa ni un porcentaje de error tolerable inventado. Una graduación pequeña no prueba exactitud de entrega; el software no certifica un dispositivo.

`dose_phase=initial` no exige antecedentes ficticios. `repeat` exige recuento entero, dosis previa real en microgramos, pauta previa y minutos transcurridos. Se comprueba la dosis anterior según la fuente declarada, incluyendo una banda RCUK previa cuando corresponda; ello no cambia la pauta ponderal actual. Un antecedente fuera de esas dos pautas necesita conciliación, no se declara incorrecto clínicamente por desconocerse aquí.

La repetición habitual es a **5 min**, según evolución. Con un intervalo menor, el contrato devuelve **apoyo de decisión urgente sin dosis, volumen, concentración ni preparación**, incluso si se declara una decisión experta excepcional. El acta previa CLI-06/TC-09 pedía no bloquear la actuación urgente; se cumple manteniendo orientación y decisión médica individual, sin convertir esa regla de flujo en evidencia para una repetición numérica anticipada. No se acepta tiempo cero ni se generan dosis sucesivas automáticamente. Desde dos dosis previas se exige escalada experta activa; se permite continuar IM mientras se organiza una perfusión segura, pero no una repetición automática con la perfusión ya funcionando.

La casilla genérica de contraindicación absoluta se reemplaza por evaluación de riesgos. No debe interpretarse una contraindicación relativa o una preocupación por excipientes como razón automática para omitir adrenalina IM ante anafilaxia vital. Revisar producto, interacciones, comorbilidad, aguja, lugar de administración y monitorización tan pronto como sea posible.

## Contrato IV: inicio de anafilaxia refractaria

Selección: adultos o niños con **compromiso respiratorio/circulatorio persistente tras dos dosis IM adecuadas**. No basta contar dosis o persistencia de urticaria. Se introducen cantidades, pautas y tiempos de las dos últimas dosis; se comprueban edad/peso, orden temporal e intervalo. Si ambas dosis están separadas por menos de 5 min, se ofrece apoyo de decisión para conciliación urgente sin emitir dosis o velocidad de perfusión; una declaración de excepción no acredita por sí sola la pauta de la fuente. La separación de población adulta a partir de 18 años solo clasifica el formulario y no altera la fórmula.

Preparación seleccionada: **1 mg de adrenalina hasta volumen FINAL de 100 mL con NaCl 0,9% = 10 microgramos/mL**. Desde producto de 1 mg/mL se extrae 1 mL. Corregir volumen de fármaco y sobrellenado real; una bolsa nominal de 100 mL más 1 mL no demuestra volumen final de 100 mL. No sustituir por 1 mg/10 mL, 1 mg/1000 mL, otra masa/volumen equivalente o glucosa 5% sin una conciliación distinta.

El experto selecciona gravedad **moderada: 0,5 mL/kg/h** o **grave con hipotensión/hipoxia: 1 mL/kg/h**, conforme a los puntos iniciales descritos en RCUK. El contrato calcula el inicio; la titulación posterior es individual al menor efecto necesario. No inventa escalones ni un máximo universal. El equilibrio tras cambios puede tardar 5–10 min. Revisar y reducir/detener ante toxicidad significativa; vigilar extravasación. Los bolos IV, otros vasopresores y la retirada no forman parte de este cálculo inicial.

Para coeficiente inicial `R` en mL/kg/h:

`bomba mL/h = W × R`; `microgramos/h = bomba × 10`; `microgramos/min = microgramos/h / 60`.

Por kg, 0,5 mL/kg/h equivale exactamente a **0,083333… microgramos/kg/min**, y 1 mL/kg/h a **0,166666…**. No etiquetar el primero como 0,1 exacto. A 70 kg, inicio moderado: **35 mL/h = 350 microgramos/h = 5,833333… microgramos/min**. `dose` expresa microgramos/min totales; la tasa por kg figura separadamente. No se asigna duración finita ni se presenta la bolsa completa como dosis administrada.

Requisitos operativos: profesional experimentado presente, bomba capaz, línea dedicada cebada y permeable, manguito de PA en otro brazo, ECG/SpO2 continuos, PA al menos cada 5 min, inspección del acceso y respuesta a complicaciones. La solución se prepara para uso inmediato y requiere comprobar producto/diluyente/recipiente/luz/asepsia. Se comparan tiempo desde preparación y límite individual verificado; al alcanzar el límite no se emite el cálculo. **No existe una vida útil universal de 24 h**. La seguridad microbiológica y el tiempo de uso no se deducen de estabilidad fisicoquímica ni de la duración teórica de la bolsa.

Si no puede administrarse con seguridad la perfusión, continuar atención y adrenalina IM cuando esté indicada, con ayuda experta. La indisponibilidad de recursos no autoriza un bolo IV ni debe retrasar reanimación. El contrato no exige un hospital específico; exige capacidades presentes.

## Evidencia técnica de esta entrega

Ejecución observada: `python -m unittest discover -s clinical/tests -p test_acute_reviewed_anaphylaxis.py -v`: **21 pruebas, OK**. Incluye positivos inicial/repetición/perfusión, ausencia de mínimo, microvolúmenes, unidades, concentraciones erróneas, cronología, edad, datos faltantes/inactivos, pediatría, recursos, caducidad y resultados no finitos.

Los tres casos completos para API/navegador están en `BROWSER_ACCEPTANCE_CASES`, dentro de `clinical/tests/test_acute_reviewed_anaphylaxis.py`, con expectativas literales calculadas a mano. El dispositivo y el límite de 60 min de esos fixtures son declaraciones sintéticas, no productos certificados ni una recomendación de estabilidad. Estas pruebas no demuestran entrega física exacta, validación diagnóstica, seguridad prospectiva ni equivalencia regulatoria internacional.

result.monitoring_and_warnings:
- Diagnose clinically when there is sudden compatible **airway, breathing or circulation compromise**, with or without skin/mucosal findings, after a likely trigger. Skin signs may be absent. Remove/stop the trigger if immediately feasible and call for resuscitation help.
- **Adrenaline (epinephrine) IM is first-line.** Inject into the anterolateral thigh using **1 mg/mL (1:1000)** solution. RCUK/ERC 2025 adult dose: **500 micrograms IM (0.5 mL)**. Repeat after **5 min** if airway/breathing/circulation problems persist.
- Pediatric age-banded IM doses from the RCUK full anaphylaxis guideline (2021, still the latest full guideline on the official current listing; distinct from the 2025 special-circumstances update): >12 y **500 micrograms**; 6--12 y **300 micrograms**; 6 months--6 y **150 micrograms**; <6 months **100--150 micrograms**. Use weight/local pediatric charts when available and independently double-check small-volume doses.
- **Reviewed IM pathway for infants under 6 months (owner acceptance 2026-11-16):** for clinically diagnosed acute anaphylaxis with ongoing airway/breathing/circulation compromise, use verified current weight: **0.01 mg/kg = 10 micrograms/kg = 0.01 mL/kg of UNDILUTED 1 mg/mL adrenaline**, injected into the anterolateral mid-thigh. This selects the weight-based recommendation in [ERC Paediatric Life Support 2025](https://www.erc.edu/media/03xnpjmj/gl2025-09-pls-e.pdf) and [WAO Anaphylaxis Guidance 2020](https://www.worldallergyorganizationjournal.org/article/S1939-4551%2820%2930375-6/fulltext). The general single-dose ceiling is 0.5 mg; it is not a minimum or an expected infant dose. The RCUK <6-month band of **100--150 micrograms** remains a documented alternative, not a floor imposed on the weight-based calculation. Reassess at 5 min; an earlier repeat is an individual expert decision outside this numerical regimen. The software keeps urgent decision support accessible but supplies no calculated repeat dose before 5 min. Confirm a device capable of accurately delivering the exact volume; no automatic rounding or dilution. **Do not dilute this IM dose to 0.1 mg/mL**: that concentration belongs to separate IV pathways. Neonatal anaphylaxis requires individual assessment; this contract does not cover resuscitation at birth or cardiac arrest. Two appropriate IM doses with continuing compromise trigger expert refractory assessment, while IM can continue as indicated until a safe infusion is running. Details and source reconciliation: [reviewed anaphylaxis contracts](../references/acute-anaphylaxis-reviewed-2026-11-16.md).
- **IM adrenaline has no absolute contraindication in anaphylaxis.** Review risks, interactions and product identity without delaying first-line treatment; relative contraindications must not become a blanket software stop.
- Position flat with or without leg elevation unless breathing difficulty requires sitting; in pregnancy use left lateral tilt/positioning as appropriate. Give high-flow oxygen and monitoring.
- **Fluids:** give IV isotonic crystalloid early for shock and reassess. RCUK adult reference bolus **500--1000 mL**; children **10 mL/kg**, repeated according to response and overload risk.
- Progressive airway edema requires early expert airway planning. Do not delay IM adrenaline while preparing the airway.
- **Refractory anaphylaxis:** persistent airway/breathing/circulation compromise after **2 appropriate IM adrenaline doses** should trigger the refractory-anaphylaxis pathway and expert **low-dose IV adrenaline infusion** with continuous monitoring. Avoid unmonitored IV adrenaline boluses.
- Antihistamines and corticosteroids are not substitutes for IM adrenaline in life-threatening anaphylaxis. Treat bronchospasm or other persistent features as adjuncts only after adrenaline/resuscitation priorities are addressed.
- **Accepted refractory infusion reference (owner acceptance 2026-11-13):** adrenaline **1 mg made up to a final volume of 100 mL with NaCl 0.9% = 10 micrograms/mL**. Start **0.5--1 mL/kg/h**, titrating to response at the lowest effective rate under experienced critical-care supervision. Calculation: 10 micrograms/mL x 0.5--1 mL/kg/h / 60 = **0.083--0.167 micrograms/kg/min**. Continue IM adrenaline every 5 min until the infusion is running. Prime the dedicated pump line; do not piggy-back or use the arm with a BP cuff. Continuous ECG/SpO2 and frequent BP, with regular cannula/extravasation checks, are mandatory. Product-specific preparation, stability and replacement interval remain subject to verification; acceptance does not certify these details.
- **Reviewed IV initiation (owner acceptance 2026-11-16):** the selected [RCUK 2021 section 6.6 regimen](https://www.resus.org.uk/sites/default/files/2021-05/Emergency%20Treatment%20of%20Anaphylaxis%20May%202021_0.pdf) applies to adults and children with persistent respiratory/circulatory compromise after two appropriate IM doses. Use **0.5 mL/kg/h for moderate severity** or **1 mL/kg/h for severe hypotensive/hypoxic presentations**, with the already specified **1 mg made up to a final volume of 100 mL** preparation. These equal **0.083333... and 0.166666... micrograms/kg/min** respectively. The calculation covers an expert-selected starting rate; it does not impose 1 mL/kg/h as a universal maintenance maximum or generate automatic titration. If the two preceding IM doses were separated by less than 5 min, provide urgent expert decision support without a calculated IV initiation rate. Verify actual prior doses/times, product-specific compatibility and use limit, pump, dedicated primed line, continuous ECG/SpO2, BP at least every 5 min and surveillance for extravasation. Details: [reviewed anaphylaxis contracts](../references/acute-anaphylaxis-reviewed-2026-11-16.md).
- **Observation/discharge (NICE NG258, 2026):** consider **2 h** observation after airway swelling has resolved and breathing, BP and HR have normalized only with a prompt response within 5--10 min to one IM dose administered within 30 min of onset, complete resolution, two in-date auto-injectors with demonstrated use and adequate adult supervision if needed. Observe at least **6 h after all symptoms resolve** if two IM doses were needed or there is previous biphasic anaphylaxis. Observe at least **12 h after all symptoms resolve** for severe reactions requiring >2 doses, severe asthma/respiratory compromise, continuing allergen absorption, out-of-hours presentation, inability to respond to deterioration or difficult emergency access. These are risk-based minima, not automatic discharge deadlines; refractory cases need critical-care assessment.
- Before discharge: provide written recurrence/emergency advice, trigger avoidance, two appropriate adrenaline auto-injectors with training when indicated and specialist allergy referral. The owner accepts this reference pathway on 2026-11-13; no named pharmacy sign-off, local stock audit or independently verified referral availability is inferred. The owner reconfirmed release of the reviewed contracts on 2026-11-16: the prior permanent software blocks are superseded by case-specific input, preparation and monitoring checks. This does not certify prospective clinical deployment.

contract_review.body:
# Anafilaxia: contratos revisados de IM en menores de 6 meses y perfusión IV

**Revisión focal: 16/11/2026.** Contratos: `anaphylaxis-under6months` y `anaphylaxis-refractory`. Núcleo internacional, sin país u hospital obligatorios. Aplicar [la política de guías internacionales](international-guideline-policy.md); las fuentes se seleccionan por alcance y calidad, no por la ubicación del propietario.

## Aceptación y procedencia

Juan ha autorizado resolver estos contratos y ha declarado su validación clínica en esta sesión. La presente entrega registra esa aceptación del propietario; no inventa una firma independiente de Farmacia/Pediatría, una auditoría de existencias ni una evaluación prospectiva. El estado global `CLINICALLY_PENDING` se conserva. Los controles individuales que se describen abajo siguen siendo necesarios.

Base comunicada por coordinación: `062d890b4fc92369b83c87664bb4bb0205ccb33f`, repositorio `JuanCopado/Emergency`. Se reutilizó material de:

- `review/anaphylaxis-under6months-evidence-20261116` en `e9855dbd37409189757c94900ee03e06ef25af3d`: conciliación de fuentes, acta funcional, preflight de microvolumen y revisión de selección de aguja. Su aclaración final diferencia IM sin diluir de la dilución IV de 1 mg hasta 10 mL.
- `review/anaphylaxis-refractory-20261116` en `0bff44dded89ea9da7f178ddf526d44969586c9c`: conciliación C04 y anexo pediátrico/pruebas negativas. La receta de perfusión ya figura en el módulo con aceptación del propietario de 13/11/2026.

Esos antecedentes documentaban cálculos o escenarios aún bloqueados. No se convierten retrospectivamente sus casos `NOT_RUN` en pruebas superadas. Esta entrega añade cálculo y comprobaciones propias; la integración en API/UI y la publicación se verifican por coordinación. Las exigencias históricas de un centro concreto no se trasladan al núcleo internacional.

## Fuentes primarias y decisión

| Fuente | Versión y uso en esta entrega |
|---|---|
| [ERC Paediatric Life Support](https://www.erc.edu/media/03xnpjmj/gl2025-09-pls-e.pdf) | 2025, Resuscitation 215:110767; sección de anafilaxia, p. 20. Fuente principal de la pauta IM ponderal y reevaluación/repetición a 5 min. Población pediátrica desde el nacimiento hasta 18 años; la reanimación al nacimiento pertenece a otro algoritmo. |
| [WAO Anaphylaxis Guidance](https://www.worldallergyorganizationjournal.org/article/S1939-4551%2820%2930375-6/fulltext) | 2020; tratamiento agudo y tabla 6. Respalda 0,01 mg/kg y ausencia de contraindicación absoluta para adrenalina IM en anafilaxia. Aporta alcance internacional; su intervalo de 5–15 min no sustituye el intervalo de 5 min seleccionado de ERC. |
| [RCUK Emergency treatment of anaphylaxis](https://www.resus.org.uk/sites/default/files/2021-05/Emergency%20Treatment%20of%20Anaphylaxis%20May%202021_0.pdf) | Mayo de 2021; tabla de dosis IM, sección 6.6 y apéndice 3. ## Contrato IM: selección, cálculo y controles

Ámbito: anafilaxia aguda diagnosticada por el profesional con compromiso ABC persistente, edad cronológica **0 a menos de 6 meses** y peso actual verificado. No diagnostica automáticamente anafilaxia ni cubre parada cardíaca o reanimación al nacimiento. Los neonatos/prematuros precisan valoración individual y ayuda adecuada sin retrasar el tratamiento necesario.

Se selecciona **10 microgramos/kg IM de adrenalina 1 mg/mL SIN DILUIR**, en cara anterolateral del tercio medio del muslo. El techo general ERC/WAO es 500 microgramos por dosis; no es un mínimo ni una dosis esperada en un lactante. La banda RCUK de **100–150 microgramos** para menores de 6 meses queda explícita como otra recomendación. No se promedian las pautas, no se impone 100 microgramos como suelo y no se sustituye el cálculo por una edad de referencia.

Para peso `W` en kg:

`microgramos = min(10 × W, 500)`; `mg = microgramos / 1000`; `mL IM = mg / 1 mg/mL`.

Ejemplo sintético: **5 kg → 50 microgramos → 0,05 mg → 0,05 mL**. No diluir a **0,1 mg/mL** para facilitar la medida: 1 mg hasta 10 mL pertenece a un circuito IV distinto. Tampoco usar la perfusión de 10 microgramos/mL como preparación IM.

La medición requiere intervalo de entrega, capacidad, incremento y exactitud del dispositivo verificados. Se calcula con `Decimal`; si el volumen exacto no puede representarse, se detiene ese cálculo operativo para revisar el método de medida. No se autoriza redondeo, dosis mínima, dilución alternativa ni un porcentaje de error tolerable inventado. Una graduación pequeña no prueba exactitud de entrega; el software no certifica un dispositivo.

`dose_phase=initial` no exige antecedentes ficticios. `repeat` exige recuento entero, dosis previa real en microgramos, pauta previa y minutos transcurridos. Se comprueba la dosis anterior según la fuente declarada, incluyendo una banda RCUK previa cuando corresponda; ello no cambia la pauta ponderal actual. Un antecedente fuera de esas dos pautas necesita conciliación, no se declara incorrecto clínicamente por desconocerse aquí.

La repetición habitual es a **5 min**, según evolución. Con un intervalo menor, el contrato devuelve **apoyo de decisión urgente sin dosis, volumen, concentración ni preparación**, incluso si se declara una decisión experta excepcional. El acta previa CLI-06/TC-09 pedía no bloquear la actuación urgente; se cumple manteniendo orientación y decisión médica individual, sin convertir esa regla de flujo en evidencia para una repetición numérica anticipada. No se acepta tiempo cero ni se generan dosis sucesivas automáticamente. Desde dos dosis previas se exige escalada experta activa; se permite continuar IM mientras se organiza una perfusión segura, pero no una repetición automática con la perfusión ya funcionando.

La casilla genérica de contraindicación absoluta se reemplaza por evaluación de riesgos. No debe interpretarse una contraindicación relativa o una preocupación por excipientes como razón automática para omitir adrenalina IM ante anafilaxia vital. Revisar producto, interacciones, comorbilidad, aguja, lugar de administración y monitorización tan pronto como sea posible.

## Contrato IV: inicio de anafilaxia refractaria

Selección: adultos o niños con **compromiso respiratorio/circulatorio persistente tras dos dosis IM adecuadas**. No basta contar dosis o persistencia de urticaria. Se introducen cantidades, pautas y tiempos de las dos últimas dosis; se comprueban edad/peso, orden temporal e intervalo. Si ambas dosis están separadas por menos de 5 min, se ofrece apoyo de decisión para conciliación urgente sin emitir dosis o velocidad de perfusión; una declaración de excepción no acredita por sí sola la pauta de la fuente. La separación de población adulta a partir de 18 años solo clasifica el formulario y no altera la fórmula.

Preparación seleccionada: **1 mg de adrenalina hasta volumen FINAL de 100 mL con NaCl 0,9% = 10 microgramos/mL**. Desde producto de 1 mg/mL se extrae 1 mL. Corregir volumen de fármaco y sobrellenado real; una bolsa nominal de 100 mL más 1 mL no demuestra volumen final de 100 mL. No sustituir por 1 mg/10 mL, 1 mg/1000 mL, otra masa/volumen equivalente o glucosa 5% sin una conciliación distinta.

El experto selecciona gravedad **moderada: 0,5 mL/kg/h** o **grave con hipotensión/hipoxia: 1 mL/kg/h**, conforme a los puntos iniciales descritos en RCUK. El contrato calcula el inicio; la titulación posterior es individual al menor efecto necesario. No inventa escalones ni un máximo universal. El equilibrio tras cambios puede tardar 5–10 min. Revisar y reducir/detener ante toxicidad significativa; vigilar extravasación. Los bolos IV, otros vasopresores y la retirada no forman parte de este cálculo inicial.

Para coeficiente inicial `R` en mL/kg/h:

`bomba mL/h = W × R`; `microgramos/h = bomba × 10`; `microgramos/min = microgramos/h / 60`.

Por kg, 0,5 mL/kg/h equivale exactamente a **0,083333… microgramos/kg/min**, y 1 mL/kg/h a **0,166666…**. No etiquetar el primero como 0,1 exacto. A 70 kg, inicio moderado: **35 mL/h = 350 microgramos/h = 5,833333… microgramos/min**. `dose` expresa microgramos/min totales; la tasa por kg figura separadamente. No se asigna duración finita ni se presenta la bolsa completa como dosis administrada.

Requisitos operativos: profesional experimentado presente, bomba capaz, línea dedicada cebada y permeable, manguito de PA en otro brazo, ECG/SpO2 continuos, PA al menos cada 5 min, inspección del acceso y respuesta a complicaciones. La solución se prepara para uso inmediato y requiere comprobar producto/diluyente/recipiente/luz/asepsia. Se comparan tiempo desde preparación y límite individual verificado; al alcanzar el límite no se emite el cálculo. **No existe una vida útil universal de 24 h**. La seguridad microbiológica y el tiempo de uso no se deducen de estabilidad fisicoquímica ni de la duración teórica de la bolsa.

Si no puede administrarse con seguridad la perfusión, continuar atención y adrenalina IM cuando esté indicada, con ayuda experta. La indisponibilidad de recursos no autoriza un bolo IV ni debe retrasar reanimación. El contrato no exige un hospital específico; exige capacidades presentes.

## Evidencia técnica de esta entrega

Ejecución observada: `python -m unittest discover -s clinical/tests -p test_acute_reviewed_anaphylaxis.py -v`: **21 pruebas, OK**. Incluye positivos inicial/repetición/perfusión, ausencia de mínimo, microvolúmenes, unidades, concentraciones erróneas, cronología, edad, datos faltantes/inactivos, pediatría, recursos, caducidad y resultados no finitos.

Los tres casos completos para API/navegador están en `BROWSER_ACCEPTANCE_CASES`, dentro de `clinical/tests/test_acute_reviewed_anaphylaxis.py`, con expectativas literales calculadas a mano. El dispositivo y el límite de 60 min de esos fixtures son declaraciones sintéticas, no productos certificados ni una recomendación de estabilidad. Estas pruebas no demuestran entrega física exacta, validación diagnóstica, seguridad prospectiva ni equivalencia regulatoria internacional.
